dropped.finding: A timed-out (rc 124) or failed reflog expiry never updates the stamp, so _reflog_expiry_due stays True and the expiry runs again on every later write, with no backoff. If the expiry keeps timing out (stalled volume, slow huge reflog), each write holds the store write lock up to an extra 30 s. If it keeps failing, each write starts an extra git process, which is the per-write cost the daily throttle was added to avoid.
scenarios: The reflog expiry times out on every pass: every write adds 30 s of lock hold, and peer writers waiting about 30 s x 2 time out.
A persistent rc!=0 failure (e.g. a ref lock left by a non-rebar git) adds a git spawn plus a WARNING to every write.
